Hi all — attaching the initial evidence set per Soojin's list. Attachments included:

1) redwood_inference_isolation_diagram_v3.pdf (high-level annotated network diagram; control plane and data plane labeled; dedicated pool / private VPC overlays shown).
2) tenant_isolation_matrix_2027-03.csv (controls -> implementation mapping; includes sample config paths, policy IDs).
3) control_descriptions_PRIVATE_DEDICATED.md (1.5 pages; explains design decisions around KMS boundaries, cross-tenant egress policing, and model artifact scoping).
4) kv_cache_and_batching_notes.txt (notes on prefix/KV caching behavior and why cross-tenant state is impossible — includes TTL/namespace details).

A few clarifications in the narrative:
- Control plane is explicitly multitenant only for control signals (deployments, metrics). Customer secrets and model artifact storage are kept in per-tenant KMS-wrapped buckets or customer-managed KMS where required.
- Dedicated pools are physically isolated GPU pools with separate tenancy metadata and network ACLs that prevent talk to other customer runtime groups; we add a soft-guard of per-tenant runtime labels and egress policies enforced at the hypervisor/network boundary.
- Private (VPC) deployments run a customer-managed control plane proxy; data plane stays within customer VPC via private peering/VPN; our documentation explains the handshake and KMS key exchange.

If the auditor needs packet-level evidence or configuration extracts we can provide redacted snippets (config lines with placeholders) under an NDA.
